docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Configures the command-line argument parser, validates input parameters, prepares execution context state, detects LLM provider configuration, instantiates the processing pipeline flow, executes it synchronously, and handles optional post-execution artifact teardown.

Under the hood, main() performs the following sequential actions: 1. Argument Parsing: Uses argparse.ArgumentParser to define and parse inputs, enforcing mutual exclusivity between --repo and --dir. 2. Flag Harmonization & Validation: - Resolves documentation generation modes (--advanced backwards-compatibility alias vs. --mode). - Validates that --incremental mode is only active when --mode api-reference is set, automatically disabling it with a terminal warning if mismatched. - Handles cache invalidation for --force-rebuild by computing the cache manifest path (.doc_cache_manifest.json) and deleting it if found. 3. State Initialization (shared): Assembles the core mutable state dictionary that flows between all nodes in the pipeline (see flow and nodes). 4. LLM Provider Detection & Logging Setup: Inspects environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_PROJECT_ID, GEMINI_API_KEY) to determine model endpoints, queries the dynamic token limit via get_model_context_length from utils.call_llm, and initializes per-run logging via configure_logging. 5. Flow Execution: Invokes create_tutorial_flow() from flow and triggers tutorial_flow.run(shared). 6. Teardown: If --cleanup was specified, purges llm_cache.json and the runtime log directory.

Parameters: None (Reads directly from sys.argv and system environment variables).

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised by argparse.ArgumentParser on parameter syntax errors, missing mandatory arguments, or when --help is invoked. * Exception: Propagates pipeline errors originating during flow execution in nodes or LLM calls in utils.call_llm.

docs.title: 1. Argument Parsing & Mode Resolution
docs.text:
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Create mutually exclusive group for source
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="english", help="Language for the generated tutorial (default: english)")
    parser.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-abstractions", type=int, default=10, help="Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-level",
        default=None,
        help="Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically)."
    )

    # --- Documentation Mode & Generation Styles ---
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"],
        default="tutorial",
        help="Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--advanced", action="store_true", help="Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced")
    parser.add_argument("--mkdocs", action="store_true", help="Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--incremental", action="store_true", help="Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force-rebuild", action="store_true", help="Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)"
    )

    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50)")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size")
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output")

    args = parser.parse_args()

The argument parser establishes strict exclusivity between remote GitHub repositories (--repo) and local directory analysis (--dir). It configures documentation generation styling (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), MkDocs integration compatibility flags, batching parameters for large codebases exceeding single-prompt context limits, reasoning effort indicators (--thinking-level), and MD5 incremental caching parameters.

docs.title: 2. Incremental Constraint Enforcement & Force Rebuild
docs.text:
# Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print(
            "\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n"
        )
        args.incremental = False

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        project_name = args.name
        if not project_name:
            # Derive project name the same way FetchRepo does
            if args.dir:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
            elif args.repo:
                project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if project_name:
            output_base = args.output or "output"
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                os.remove(manifest_path)
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] Deleted cache manifest: {manifest_path}\033[0m")
            else:
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] No cache manifest found at {manifest_path} — all chapters will be generated fresh.\033[0m")
    elif args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        print("\033[93m[Warning] --force-rebuild has no effect without --incremental. Ignoring.\033[0m")

Because incremental MD5 generation relies on a 1:1 mapping between source files and output Markdown documentation (a feature unique to api-reference mode), main() guards against invalid configurations by disabling incremental caching if requested under holistic modes like tutorial or advanced. When --force-rebuild is supplied alongside --incremental, the manifest .doc_cache_manifest.json located within the target output directory is detected and unlinked, guaranteeing that stale hashes are discarded.

docs.title: 3. Shared Context Assembly
docs.text:
# Prepare shared store to be passed between nodes
    shared = {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,  # Can be None, FetchRepo will derive it
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Add include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Add language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Add use_cache flag (inverse of no-cache flag)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Add max_abstraction_num parameter
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # Add thinking_level for LLM reasoning capabilities
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        # Add max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Added mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": doc_mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": doc_mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs will be populated by the nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The shared dictionary is initialized as the centralized blackboard state for the PocketFlow engine. It captures input flags, normalizes include/exclude pattern sets (combining user exclusions with DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS), and pre-allocates intermediate data slots (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) that pipeline nodes populate downstream.

docs.title: 4. Provider Resolution, Logging, & Execution
docs.text:
# Get LLM configuration for display
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown")
        endpoint_url = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        # Fallback to Gemini if neither provider is explicitly set but it's used
        if os.environ.get("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            provider = "GEMINI"
            model_name = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
            endpoint_url = "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
            api_key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
        else:
            provider = "UNKNOWN"
            model_name = "unknown"
            endpoint_url = "unknown"
            api_key = ""

    from utils.call_llm import configure_logging, get_model_context_length

    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)

    # Derive project name for logging (before flow runs, which may override shared["project_name"])
    if args.name:
        log_project_name = args.name
    elif args.dir:
        log_project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(args.dir))
    elif args.repo:
        log_project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
    else:
        log_project_name = "project"

    # Configure per-run logging: logs/{project}_{mode}_{datetime}.log
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=log_project_name, mode=doc_mode)

    # ... Display configuration print blocks ...

    # Create the flow instance
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

    # Run the flow
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

The resolution block checks environment variables to determine which provider backend is configured (such as OpenAI-compatible endpoints or Google Gemini). It then queries get_model_context_length from utils.call_llm to dynamically compute model window capacities for chunking decisions. Logging is initialized via configure_logging to write to a timestamped file under the configured log directory. Finally, create_tutorial_flow is called to instantiate the workflow, followed by tutorial_flow.run(shared) to synchronously execute the node graph.

docs.title: 5. Post-Run Cleanup Logic
docs.text:
# Cleanup logs and cache if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        print("\nCleaning up cache and logs...")
        cache_path = "llm_cache.json"
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                print(f" - Removed {cache_path}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f" - Failed to remove {cache_path}: {e}")

        log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
        if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
            import shutil

            try:
                shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
                print(f" - Removed {log_dir} directory")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f" - Failed to remove {log_dir}: {e}")

If the --cleanup flag is passed, this block executes after pipeline completion. It attempts to remove local ephemeral files created during LLM invocations (llm_cache.json) and recursively deletes the run log directory (defaulting to logs/ or the path specified by LOG_DIR), catching and reporting any filesystem I/O exceptions without crashing the main process.

if __name__ == "__main__":

docs.title: main.py
docs.text:
Source: main.py

This module serves as the primary Command-Line Interface (CLI) bootstrap, configuration parser, and runtime orchestrator for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder documentation pipeline. While flow.py defines the directed acyclic graph (DAG) structure and node lifecycles under the PocketFlow framework, main.py initializes the execution environment, parses and validates user-supplied flags, resolves environment-based LLM configurations, constructs the global shared store, and executes the compiled pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
main.py provides an end-to-end operational harness for processing either remote GitHub repositories or local directory structures into structured technical documentation. Its execution lifecycle consists of several distinct stages:

  1. Environment & Argument Parsing: Reads local environment variables via python-dotenv, parses CLI flags via argparse.ArgumentParser, and sets up global terminal output strategies via utils.output.init.
  2. Mode & Entity Resolution: Normalizes documentation generation styles (e.g., resolving legacy --advanced flags into explicit --mode styles such as tutorial, advanced, api-reference, or sdk) and derives project identifiers from repository URLs or local filesystem paths.
  3. LLM Provider & Context Discovery: Inspects runtime environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_*, etc.) and determines the target LLM provider, base endpoint, model name, and context window token constraints via utils.call_llm.get_model_context_length.
  4. Validation & State Initialization: Enforces business constraints (such as restricting --incremental caching and --force-rebuild operations to api-reference mode) and initializes the shared memory dictionary (shared) used across all PocketFlow nodes.
  5. Flow Execution & Cleanup: Configures file and console logging via utils.output.configure_logging, triggers flow.create_tutorial_flow().run(shared), and executes optional cache and log purges when --cleanup is invoked.

docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments() -> tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]:

Description: Constructs and configures the CLI argument parser using Python's standard argparse module. Defines mutually exclusive source groups (--repo and --dir), output paths, inclusion/exclusion rules, context window token budgets, thinking effort parameters, generation modes, and execution flags. Returns both the parser instance (used for raising standard CLI validation errors) and the parsed Namespace object.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A 2-tuple containing the configured ArgumentParser instance and the resulting parsed Namespace containing all CLI options.

Raises: * SystemExit: Automatically triggered by argparse if unrecognized flags are passed or --help is requested.

Example: 

# From main.py: main()
parser, args = parse_arguments()
init_output(
    language=args.language,
    use_cache=not args.no_cache,
    thinking_level=args.thinking_level,
)

The parse_arguments() function configures CLI parameters across functional groups: source location (--repo, --dir), runtime maintenance (--cleanup), metadata overrides (--name, --token, --output), filtering constraints (--include, --exclude, --max-size), LLM generation behaviors (--language, --no-cache, --max-abstractions, --thinking-level, --max-tokens), documentation modes (--mode, --advanced, --mkdocs, --incremental, --force-rebuild), and execution controls (--batch, --force-batch, --debug). Mutually exclusive groups ensure users cannot pass both a remote repository URL and a local directory path simultaneously, maintaining deterministic ingest boundaries.

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Resolves the active documentation mode and extracts a normalized project name. If the legacy --advanced flag is detected, it overrides the default tutorial mode (emitting a warning if an explicit conflicting --mode was passed). If no explicit project name is supplied via -n/--name, the function derives the project name from the base directory name of --dir or the final path segment of --repo.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed CLI arguments namespace.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple of (mode, project_name).

Raises: * None internally.

Example: 

# From main.py: resolve_mode_and_project implementation
def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name

resolve_mode_and_project provides backward compatibility for legacy workflows while standardizing project naming across varied input sources. When --advanced is active alongside a conflicting --mode argument (such as --mode api-reference), the function invokes emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE") to alert the user before forcing the mode string to "advanced". If the project name is omitted, it parses local directory paths via os.path.abspath to resolve relative references (like .), strips trailing slashes from GitHub URLs to extract repository identifiers cleanly, or defaults to the fallback string "project".

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str) -> dict[str, Any]:

Description: Constructs the central shared state dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes throughout the pipeline lifecycle. It combines CLI flags, merges custom exclusion patterns with utils.exclude_patterns.DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, inverts cache control flags, sets generation constraints, and allocates empty collection slots (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) to be populated by downstream processing nodes.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed command-line arguments. * github_token (str | None): The resolved GitHub Personal Access Token, or None if unauthenticated/local. * mode (str): The resolved documentation mode string.

Returns: * dict[str, Any]: The shared dictionary containing all configuration parameters and mutable state containers for the execution graph.

Raises: * None internally.

Example: 

# From main.py: build_shared_store implementation
def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,  # Can be None, FetchRepo will derive it
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The dictionary returned by build_shared_store serves as the sole shared state across all PocketFlow nodes in nodes.py. It unions any user-provided --exclude arguments with the built-in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS set, ensuring standard build directories, binaries, and virtual environments are excluded regardless of CLI input. It also maps flags such as --no-cache to positive boolean flags (use_cache: not args.no_cache) and creates empty mutable structures for intermediate artifacts such as extracted file representations and abstract semantic models.

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Introspects the execution environment to identify the active LLM provider, target model name, base API endpoint URL, and credentials. If LLM_PROVIDER is set, it dynamically resolves provider-prefixed environment variables (e.g., OPENROUTER_MODEL, OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, OPENROUTER_API_KEY). If unset, it falls back to Gemini detection via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY. Finally, it determines the maximum context window length by either honoring --max-tokens or invoking get_model_context_length from utils.call_llm.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed command-line arguments (used to check for explicit max_tokens overrides).

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple containing (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length).

Raises: * None internally; unresolvable configurations return placeholder "unknown" values and fallback token lengths.

Example: 

# From main.py: detect_llm_config implementation
def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.call_llm import get_model_context_length

    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown")
        endpoint_url = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        # Fallback to Gemini if neither provider is explicitly set but it's used
        if os.environ.get("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            provider = "GEMINI"
            model_name = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
            endpoint_url = "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
            api_key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
        else:
            provider = "UNKNOWN"
            model_name = "unknown"
            endpoint_url = "unknown"
            api_key = ""

    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length

detect_llm_config implements provider detection logic that supports both OpenAI-compatible endpoints and Google AI / Vertex AI infrastructure. When LLM_PROVIDER is specified (e.g., OLLAMA or OPENROUTER), it extracts the associated environment variables based on that prefix. When no generic provider is declared, it inspects Gemini-specific environment variables, defaulting to gemini-3.7-flash and Google's endpoint. The context length calculation defers to args.max_tokens when explicitly set by the user, bypassing network lookups in get_model_context_length.

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str) -> None:

Description: Formats and emits the active runtime configuration to the console using the localized emit and get functions from utils.output. Displays details including the repository/directory target, AI provider, endpoint, model name, context window token limit, thinking effort level, batch size, output mode, MkDocs integration status, incremental caching status, and log file destination.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed CLI arguments namespace. * mode (str): The resolved documentation mode string. * provider (str): The detected LLM provider name. * model_name (str): The active LLM model identifier. * endpoint_url (str): The active LLM endpoint URL. * context_length (int): The maximum context window size in tokens. * log_file (str): The absolute or relative path to the active execution log file.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * None internally.

Example: 

# From main.py: display_config implementation
def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block

display_config standardizes user-facing startup diagnostics by routing all terminal output through the localization template engine in utils.output. It handles mode-specific discrepancies—such as reflecting that max_abstractions is dynamically computed from discovered code modules when running in api-reference mode rather than fixed to a numeric limit. It also formats boolean parameters (such as force_batch, mkdocs, and incremental) into localized Enabled/Disabled strings retrieved via get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED") and get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED").

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Performs filesystem cleanup operations by deleting persisted LLM disk cache files and clearing the runtime log directory. Iterates through known cache paths (llm_cache.json) and removes the directory indicated by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to ./logs). Emits detailed event logs tracking each deleted artifact and catches filesystem errors to prevent cleanup failures from raising unhandled exceptions.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * Catches all Exception instances during file unlinking and directory tree removal, routing error descriptions through emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", ...).

Example: 

# From main.py: _run_cleanup implementation
def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    import shutil

    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in ["llm_cache.json"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

_run_cleanup manages filesystem maintenance tasks when invoked via --cleanup (either standalone or as a post-generation step). It targets the persistent cache file (llm_cache.json) generated by utils.call_llm and uses shutil.rmtree to remove accumulated pipeline execution logs. All file deletion operations are wrapped in try/except blocks to guard against permission issues or file lock contention on Windows environments, emitting localized notifications for each outcome.

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: The primary entry point and orchestrator for the application. Coordinates argument parsing, output subsystem initialization, source verification, token resolution, mode normalization, constraint validation, shared memory initialization, LLM detection, logging configuration, diagnostic display, PocketFlow graph instantiation, pipeline execution, and post-execution cleanup.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Exits with status 1 if --force-rebuild is supplied without --incremental, or via parser.error() if neither --repo, --dir, nor --cleanup is provided.

Example: 

# From main.py: main implementation
def main():
    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=args.thinking_level,
    )

    # Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    // ... [Token resolution, mode checks, and store creation]

    shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)

    # Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

    # Cleanup after run if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        _run_cleanup()

The main() function contains the execution rules for running the pipeline:

  1. Standalone Maintenance: Checks if --cleanup was passed without repository or directory sources; if so, it purges cache and log files and terminates immediately.
  2. Authentication Handling: Inspects -t/--token and the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable. Emits warnings if a remote repository lacks a token (which may lead to GitHub API rate limits) or if a token was supplied for a local directory analysis.
  3. Incremental Cache Enforcement: Verifies that --incremental is only used with mode == "api-reference", falling back to non-incremental execution with a warning otherwise. If --force-rebuild is enabled, it deletes the incremental cache manifest (.doc_cache_manifest.json) from the output directory before triggering the flow.
  4. Execution & Teardown: Instantiates the flow graph via create_tutorial_flow() and invokes its .run(shared) method. If --cleanup was passed alongside generation arguments, it executes _run_cleanup() after the flow completes.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The nodes.py module serves as the primary execution engine for Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. Built on top of the PocketFlow framework (Node and BatchNode), it defines the graph computation stages required to crawl a codebase, filter code files, analyze architectural abstractions, extract module relationships, determine logical chapter sequences, write comprehensive documentation chapters, and assemble the final output (either as a traditional markdown book or as an MkDocs Material documentation site).

The module supports two primary generation strategies: 1. Direct / LLM-Assisted Pipeline: Analyzes codebase topology, clusters abstractions, discovers relationships, sequences chapters, and generates tutorial/advanced documentation with cross-chapter summarization. 2. Deterministic API-Reference Pipeline: Employs an LLM-filtered deterministic mapper to produce exhaustive 1:1 API documentation for every actual code file, bypassing abstraction discovery and generating structured hierarchical navigation trees.

The workflow supports token-aware batching (via utils.token_utils and utils.call_llm), multi-language generation, and incremental MD5 content caching to prevent redundant LLM invocations.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data: list, indices: list) -> dict:

Description: Resolves file index references into a structured dictionary mapping index keys (formatted as "{index} # {path}") to file text contents. This mapping provides contextual anchors for LLM prompts when referencing files across abstractions.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): List of tuples containing relative file paths and file content strings. * indices (list[int]): List of integer indices corresponding to items in files_data.

Returns: * dict[str, str]: Mapping of index-annotated path keys to file content strings.

Raises: * None. Out-of-bounds indices are ignored via boundary verification (0 <= i < len(files_data)).

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function iterates over the target file indices, bounds-checking each index against files_data. Valid files are injected into the returned dictionary with key format f"{i} # {path}". This specific key format matches the syntax expected by the prompt templates loaded via utils.prompts.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name: str, advanced_mode: bool = False, mode: str = None) -> str:

Description: Reads Markdown prompt template files stored within the package's prompts/ directory. It selects the subdirectory based on explicit mode configuration or fallback flags, handling UTF-8-SIG encoded files cleanly.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the prompt template file (without .md extension). * advanced_mode (bool): Fallback flag used to choose between "advanced" and "tutorial" when mode is None. Defaults to False. * mode (str | None): Specific prompt mode subdirectory (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "common"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw template content read from disk.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed path does not exist. * IOError: If the file cannot be read.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

The function resolves relative path coordinates against __file__, resolving the target subdirectory dynamically. The utf-8-sig encoding ensures seamless handling of Byte Order Marks (BOM) when reading templates across different operating systems.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> dict | list:

Description: Parses structured YAML payloads returned from LLM completions that are enclosed in markdown triple-backtick code fences (```yaml).

Parameters: * response (str): Raw text response generated by the LLM.

Returns: * dict | list: Parsed Python data structure returned by yaml.safe_load.

Raises: * ValueError: If the YAML fence is missing or if yaml.safe_load fails to parse the extracted block.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

The parsing strategy splits the string strictly around the ```yaml marker and terminates at the subsequent closing ``` fence. It trims excess whitespace and processes the payload safely using yaml.safe_load(). Any parse error or fence-split failure wraps into a descriptive ValueError to trigger upstream node retries.

docs.title: create_token_counter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> Callable[[str], int]:

Description: Factory function providing a callable token counter. It initializes tiktoken with the cl100k_base encoding (OpenAI standard) and falls back to a 4-characters-per-token heuristic if tiktoken fails or is unavailable.

Returns: * Callable[[str], int]: A lambda function accepting a string and returning estimated token length.

Example: 

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

Under normal operation, the returned lambda executes len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=())) to disable special token validation exceptions. If encoding resolution raises any exception, it falls back gracefully to len(text) // 4.

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_max_tokens(shared: dict) -> int:

Description: Resolves the effective maximum context window for the current execution run. It prioritizes explicit limits configured in shared["max_tokens"], falling back to provider inspection via environment variables.

Parameters: * shared (dict): PocketFlow shared memory dictionary.

Returns: * int: Context length limit in tokens.

Example: 

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from provider env vars."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:
        endpoint = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
        model_name = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        endpoint = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "")
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)

If max_tokens is not directly provided in shared, the function inspects LLM_PROVIDER. If set to GEMINI (or omitted), it evaluates defaults for Google Gemini endpoints. For generic OpenAI-compatible providers, it constructs base URL, model name, and API key environment variable lookups and delegates context window detection to get_model_context_length from utils.call_llm.

docs.title: FetchRepo.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict:

Description: Extracts repository coordinates (repo_url, local_dir), project name, pattern filters (include_patterns, exclude_patterns), and maximum file size constraints from shared. Derives the project name if absent.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store.

Returns: * dict: Prepared parameter dictionary for file crawling.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
        local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
        project_name = shared.get("project_name")

        if not project_name:
            # Basic name derivation from URL or directory
            if repo_url:
                project_name = repo_url.split("/")[-1].replace(".git", "")
            else:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(local_dir))
            shared["project_name"] = project_name

        # Get file patterns directly from shared
        include_patterns = shared["include_patterns"]
        exclude_patterns = shared["exclude_patterns"]
        max_file_size = shared["max_file_size"]

        return {
            "repo_url": repo_url,
            "local_dir": local_dir,
            "token": shared.get("github_token"),
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "max_file_size": max_file_size,
            "use_relative_paths": True,
        }

The method sanitizes project identification by stripping .git from remote URLs or resolving directory basenames locally. It packages include/exclude glob rules and relative path configurations for exec().

docs.title: FetchRepo.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Executes either utils.crawl_github_files or utils.crawl_local_files based on the presence of repo_url. Transforms output dictionary mappings into [(path, content), ...] tuples.

Parameters: * prep_res (dict): Crawler parameters from prep().

Returns: * list[tuple[str, str]]: List of 2-element tuples containing relative file paths and string contents.

Raises: * ValueError: If crawling results in 0 matching files.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
        llm_logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}")

        if prep_res["repo_url"]:
            print(f"Crawling repository: {prep_res['repo_url']}...")
            result = crawl_github_files(
                repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
                token=prep_res["token"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )
        else:
            print(f"Crawling directory: {prep_res['local_dir']}...")

            result = crawl_local_files(
                directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )

        # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
        files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
        if len(files_list) == 0:
            raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")

        llm_logger.info(f"NODE COMPLETE | node=FetchRepo | files_found={len(files_list)}")
        return files_list

The method branches execution dynamically to either GitHub API crawling or local filesystem traversal. Output dictionaries are converted to list tuples. An explicit ValueError guard aborts the pipeline early if filtering yielded an empty file set.

docs.text: ContextRouter analyzes total prompt overhead, file token counts, and documentation mode to choose between direct, batch (map-reduce), and deterministic pipelines.

docs.title: ContextRouter._build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Static) Signature: def _build_directory_tree(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str:

Description: Constructs a compact text-based representation of the directory structure annotated with index numbers for each file.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): List of (path, content) tuples.

Returns: * str: Formatted directory tree string.

Example: 

    @staticmethod
    def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
        """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
        from collections import defaultdict

        dir_files = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
            basename = os.path.basename(path)
            dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

        lines = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
            lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
            lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
        return "\n".join(lines)

The helper groups files under their containing folder path using defaultdict(list). It sorts directories alphabetically and formats the tree with leading indents and file index tags (basename (idx:0)).

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Calculates token overhead (prompt templates, directory tree, file index listings), estimates total file tokens, determines safety margins (95% of max context), and decides the execution route (deterministic, direct, or batch).

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store.

Returns: * tuple: Prepared routing tuple including route key, file data, limits, and batch parameters.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

        # --- Token estimation setup ---
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()

        // ... [measures template, directory tree, and listing tokens to compute prompt_overhead]

        # --- Count file content tokens ---
        total_tokens = 0
        file_token_map = []
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            tokens = count_tokens(entry)
            total_tokens += tokens
            file_token_map.append(tokens)

        # --- Effective limit = safety margin minus overhead ---
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            print("\033[92m[Capacity] api-reference mode active. Bypassing LLM discovery and routing to DeterministicFileMapper.\033[0m")
            return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

        if total_tokens > effective_limit and force_batch:
            // ... [logs capacity warnings]
        // ... [checks total_tokens <= effective_limit and returns ("direct", ...) or ("batch", ...)]

prep() calculates prompt overhead by measuring template sizes across tutorial and advanced folders and adding the directory tree and file index sizes. If mode is api-reference, it immediately selects deterministic. Otherwise, if total file tokens exceed effective_limit or force_batch is set, it selects batch; otherwise, it routes to direct.

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]:

Description: If routed as direct or deterministic, returns the route string. If batch, groups files by directory and splits them into token-budgeted, non-mixing directory batches.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked parameter tuple from prep().

Returns: * str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]: Routing string or list of file batches.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
        llm_logger.info(
            f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}"
        )

        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            # Flush remaining files in this directory
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)
        // ... [logs debug batch info and saves directory tree]
        return batches

The batching algorithm organizes files by directory to preserve lexical and architectural cohesion. It prevents mixing files from different directories in the same batch, splitting a directory into sub-batches only when token counts exceed effective_limit or file count exceeds batch_size.

Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[int]) -> str:

Description: Converts valid code file indices into 1:1 module records. Injects shared["abstractions"], shared["chapter_order"], and synthetic shared["relationships"] directly into state, routing to "default".

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store. * prep_res (tuple): Result from prep(). * exec_res (list[int]): Valid code indices from exec().

Returns: * str: Returns "default".

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        import os

        files = shared.get("files", [])
        valid_indices = set(exec_res)
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, _content) in enumerate(files):
            if idx not in valid_indices:
                print(f"  - Skipping non-code file: {file_path}")
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.splitext(file_path)[0].replace(os.sep, ".").replace("/", ".")

            modules.append(
                {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
            )
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        shared["chapter_order"] = chapter_order
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        print(f"\033[92m[DeterministicFileMapper] Mapped {len(modules)} ACTUAL code files for exhaustive documentation.\033[0m")
        return "default"

The method normalizes each file's relative path into a dot-separated module identifier (e.g., utils/call_llm.py becomes utils.call_llm). Each abstraction points to a single file index via files: [idx], and chapter_order is assigned linearly.

docs.title: Class: IdentifyAbstractions
docs.text: IdentifyAbstractions is used when the entire codebase fits comfortably within the token budget. It analyzes all files in a single prompt.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Packs all files into an LLM context string, applying truncation warnings if the 95% safety margin is reached, and prepares the identify_abstractions prompt parameters.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store.

Returns: * tuple: Packed tuple containing context strings, file listings, and configuration flags.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
            count_tokens = create_token_counter()
            context = ""
            file_info = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                    break
                context += entry
                file_info.append((i, path))
                current_tokens += entry_tokens

            return context, file_info

        context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
        file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])
        return (
            context,
            file_listing_for_prompt,
            len(files_data),
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            max_abstraction_num,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )

The inner helper create_llm_context iterates through files sequentially, tracking cumulative token counts against safety_limit. If limits are exceeded, it truncates context at the boundary and returns the partial context alongside the file listing.

            )

                raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

docs.text:
AnalyzeRelationships analyzes dependencies and directional data flow between abstractions using a dynamic, two-pass token redistribution budget.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Distributes available context tokens evenly across identified abstractions in Pass 1, redistributes unused token budget to larger abstractions in Pass 2, and inlines file snippets without exceeding context limits.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store.

Returns: * tuple: Relationship prompt parameters and budgeted code contexts.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        // ... [initializes context with abstraction descriptions and token metrics]
        # Pre-compute file token sizes for all abstractions
        abstr_file_data = []
        for abstr in abstractions:
            sized = []
            for idx in abstr["files"]:
                if 0 <= idx < len(files_data):
                    path, file_content = files_data[idx]
                    entry = f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
                    sized.append((idx, path, file_content, estimate_tokens(entry)))
            sized.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
            abstr_file_data.append(sized)

        # Two-pass allocation:
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
        // ... [formats context strings and returns prep tuple]

The budgeting algorithm prevents late-stage starvation by allocating total_budget // num_abstractions to each abstraction in Pass 1. Files already included in prior abstractions are deduplicated. In Pass 2, any unspent token balance is pooled and used to include remaining files from larger abstractions.

Returns: * dict: Dictionary with keys summary (project overview text) and details (list of {"from": int, "to": int, "label": str}).

    def exec(self, prep_res):

            if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
                raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")

            validated_relationships = []
            for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
                if not isinstance(rel, dict) or not all(k in rel for k in ["from_abstraction", "to_abstraction", "label"]):
                    raise ValueError(f"Missing keys in relationship item: {rel}")

                from_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", str(rel["from_abstraction"]))[0])

                    continue
                validated_relationships.append({"from": from_idx, "to": to_idx, "label": rel["label"]})

            return {"summary": relationships_data["summary"], "details": validated_relationships}

            raise e

    def prep(self, shared):

        relationships = shared["relationships"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")

            to_name = abstractions[rel["to"]]["name"]
            context += f"- From {rel['from']} ({from_name}) to {rel['to']} ({to_name}): {rel['label']}\n"

        return (
            abstraction_listing,
            context,
            len(abstractions),
            project_name,
            "",
            use_cache,

            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),

docs.title: OrderChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Executes order_chapters.md and validates that the resulting sequence contains every abstraction index exactly once.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Sequence parameters from prep().

Returns: * list[int]: Ordered list of abstraction indices.

Raises: * ValueError: If indices are out of range, duplicated, or missing.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            (
                abstraction_listing,
                context,
                num_abstractions,
                project_name,
                list_lang_note,
                use_cache,
                thinking_level,
                _advanced_mode,
                max_tokens,
                doc_mode,
            ) = prep_res

            prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
            prompt = prompt_template.format(
                project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context
            )
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
            ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)

            ordered_indices = []
            seen_indices = set()
            for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
                idx = int(str(entry).split("#")[0].strip())
                if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions) or idx in seen_indices:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid or duplicate index: {idx}")
                ordered_indices.append(idx)
                seen_indices.add(idx)

            if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
                raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length mismatch: expected {num_abstractions}, got {len(ordered_indices)}")

            return ordered_indices
        except Exception as e:
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

docs.title: WriteChapters.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Initializes chapter summary accumulators (chapters_written_so_far, chapter_summaries), computes relative markdown links across all chapters, and builds batch payload dictionaries.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store.

Returns: * list[dict]: List of chapter generation payloads.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        self.chapters_written_so_far = []
        self.chapter_summaries = []

        all_chapters = []
        chapter_filenames = {}
        for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
            if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions):
                chapter_num = i + 1
                chapter_name = abstractions[abstraction_index]["name"].replace("\n", " ").strip()
                is_mkdocs = shared.get("mkdocs", False)
                if is_mkdocs and "original_path" in abstractions[abstraction_index]:
                    doc_rel_path = os.path.splitext(abstractions[abstraction_index]["original_path"])[0] + ".md"
                    filename = doc_rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
                elif is_mkdocs:
                    safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()
                    filename = f"{safe_name}.md"
                else:
                    safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()
                    filename = f"{i + 1:02d}_{safe_name}.md"

                all_chapters.append(f"{chapter_num}. [{chapter_name}]({filename})")
                chapter_filenames[abstraction_index] = {"num": chapter_num, "name": chapter_name, "filename": filename}
        // ... [constructs relative linking paths and returns item dicts]

prep() calculates relative markdown links (relpath) for each chapter target so cross-references resolve correctly even within nested subdirectories (e.g., docs/api/utils/call_llm.md).

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> dict:

Description: Drafts an individual chapter. Checks the MD5 cache manifest in incremental mode; on cache miss, invokes draft_chapters.md via call_llm, ensures markdown headings are formatted correctly, generates a summary via build_chapter_summary_prompt, and updates running context.

Parameters: * item (dict): Single chapter configuration from prep().

Returns: * dict: Dictionary with keys content (markdown text), hash (MD5 hex digest), and name (abstraction name).

Example: 

    def exec(self, item):
        try:
            abstraction_name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
            chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
            project_name = item.get("project_name")
            language = item.get("language", "english")
            use_cache = item.get("use_cache", True)
            thinking_level = item.get("thinking_level", None)
            doc_mode = item.get("mode", "tutorial")
            is_mkdocs = item.get("mkdocs", False)
            incremental = item.get("incremental", False)
            output_dir = item.get("output_dir", "output")
            filename = item.get("filename")
            max_tokens = item.get("max_tokens", 100000)

            file_context_str = "\n\n".join(
                f"--- File: {idx_path.split('# ')[1] if '# ' in idx_path else idx_path} ---\n{content}"
                for idx_path, content in item["related_files_content_map"].items()
            )

            # --- Incremental Caching Logic ---
            current_hash = None
            if incremental and output_dir:
                import hashlib
                import json
                hasher = hashlib.md5()
                hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
                current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()
                manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
                if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                    with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        manifest = json.load(f)
                    if manifest.get(abstraction_name) == current_hash:
                        // ... [loads cached markdown and appends to context summaries]
                        return {"content": clean_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name}

            // ... [formats draft_chapters.md and invokes call_llm]
            chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
            self.chapters_written_so_far.append(chapter_content)

            # Generate LLM summary for cross-chapter context (skip for api-reference)
            if doc_mode != "api-reference":
                summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
                chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=None)
                self.chapter_summaries.append(f"Chapter {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

            return {"content": chapter_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name}
        except Exception as e:
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

The method uses condensed 3-5 sentence LLM-generated summaries rather than full chapter dumps for cross-chapter context, avoiding $O(N^2)$ token explosion across chapters.

docs.title: WriteChapters.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list, exec_res_list: list[dict]) -> None:

Description: Saves the generated chapters list to shared["chapters"], writes updated MD5 content hashes to .doc_cache_manifest.json, and records summaries in shared["chapter_summaries"].

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state store. * prep_res (list): List of input batch items. * exec_res_list (list[dict]): Batch execution results.

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        import json
        import os

        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        if shared.get("incremental"):
            output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
            os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

            manifest = {}
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                try:
                    with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        manifest = json.load(f)
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for res in exec_res_list:
                if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                    manifest[res["name"]] = res["hash"]

            with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

        shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)
        del self.chapters_written_so_far
        del self.chapter_summaries

docs.title: Class: CombineTutorial
docs.text: CombineTutorial writes the final documentation structure to disk, generating table-of-contents indexes, Mermaid diagrams, single-page compilations, or complete MkDocs Material sites with LLM-grouped navigation.

docs.title: CombineTutorial._build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Static) Signature: def _build_index_sections(lines: list[str], sections: list[dict], chapter_files: list[dict], level: int = 3) -> None:

Description: Recursively generates nested Markdown sections containing module index tables for the MkDocs api/index.md landing page.

Parameters: * lines (list[str]): Output list of markdown lines being appended to. * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical section dictionaries returned from the navigation grouping model. * chapter_files (list[dict]): List of chapter metadata dictionaries. * level (int): Markdown header indentation level (###, ####, etc.). Defaults to 3.

Example: 

    @staticmethod
    def _build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3):
        """Recursively build index.md sections with module tables."""
        heading = "#" * level
        for section in sections:
            lines.append(f"{heading} {section['name']}")
            lines.append("")
            if section.get("modules"):
                lines.append("| Module | Description |")
                lines.append("|--------|-------------|")
                for mod_name in section["modules"]:
                    match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
                    if match:
                        display = mod_name.split(".")[-1] if "." in mod_name else mod_name
                        desc = match["description"]
                        if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
                            content_lines = match["content"].strip().split("\n")
                            for cl in content_lines:
                                cs = cl.strip()
                                if cs and not cs.startswith(("---", "#", "```", "title:", "sidebar_position:")):
                                    desc = cs[:120]
                                    break
                        lines.append(f"| [{display}](api/{match['filename']}) | {desc} |")
                lines.append("")
            for child in section.get("children", []):
                CombineTutorial._build_index_sections(lines, [child], chapter_files, level + 1)

The method renders hierarchical section headers and markdown tables. If module descriptions contain placeholder text (such as "Internal API reference for..."), it extracts the first non-empty paragraph from the generated chapter markdown.

Source: nodes.py

Following the orchestration harness established in main.py and graph structures configured in flow.py, nodes.py defines the core functional processing units of the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder documentation pipeline. It implements concrete subclasses of PocketFlow's Node and BatchNode abstractions to handle filesystem crawling, LLM prompt generation, contextual token-budgeted routing, hierarchical abstraction identification, relationship extraction, chapter authoring, and final static site artifact generation.

The module manages mutable state across a shared dictionary (shared), coordinating interactions with external LLMs via utils/call_llm.py, token accounting through utils/token_utils.py, prompt templating via utils/prompts.py, and localized CLI event broadcasting via utils/output.py.
